---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on every stop/start.

name: windows-build-on-gcp-vm
description: JusPrin builds and runs on the GCP Windows VM; the five traps that make it fail, and why the CI Windows job failing is a runner-environment problem, not a script bug.
metadata:
  type: project
---

JusPrin compiles from source on the Windows test VM and the built binary runs
with its Agent UI visible. Verified 2026-09-07 on n2-standard-16: deps 22.7 min,
slicer 23.0 min. Output is `orca-slicer.exe` (261 KB launcher) plus
`OrcaSlicer.dll` (122.7 MB). Full recipe in
`/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/BUILDING.md`; VM setup in its README.
See [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]].

**Why:** four of the five failures below produce misleading errors far from
their cause, and two were self-inflicted by how the build was driven.

**How to apply:**
- Run long builds as a Windows **scheduled task** (SYSTEM / ServiceAccount), not
  over SSH — OpenSSH kills the process tree on disconnect. Never let two builds
  share a directory: that produced OpenSSL `C1033 cannot open program database`.
- Add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` to PATH so **awk** is found, or libpng
  cannot generate `pngprefix.h` (`-DPNG_PREFIX=` in deps/PNG/PNG.cmake) and you
  get a confusing `C1083` on a header that was never written.
- Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for CMake 4.x.
- **Do not use the CI deps artifact** — the shipped bundle predates `deps/Eigen`
  and cannot satisfy Eigen 5.0.1. Build deps from source.
- Never hard-stop the VM mid-build: doing so left 622 installed files full of
  NUL bytes and surfaced as fake syntax errors inside Boost headers.
- Qhull is deliberately excluded on MSVC (deps/CMakeLists.txt), so 24/25 is
  complete on Windows.
- To run headless, use the app's own hook rather than dropping DLLs beside the
  exe: `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` when
  system OpenGL < 2.0. Still force `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`.

The `Build all` Windows CI job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is a GitHub runner
environment problem, not `build_release_vs.bat` — the same script selects the
same generator on the VM and configures fine against registered Build Tools.

**MSVC rejects `this` in a nested lambda's init-capture.** Found 2026-09-07 at
commit fbe5963b: `CallAfter([self=wxWeakRef<wxWindow>(this),...])` written INSIDE
another lambda compiled on clang but failed on MSVC with 37 errors, because MSVC
bound that `this` to the enclosing closure object, so it tried to build a
`wxWeakRef<wxWindow>` from a lambda pointer
(`Tracked_class_should_inherit_from_wxTrackable`). Name the object first —
`auto* menu = this;` then capture `menu`. Watch for this pattern whenever a
deferred callback is set up from within another lambda; it is invisible on macOS.

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

content.text:
Neither — you already have a third option working, and it's better than both. Yesterday we built a harness that lets Claude Code **on your Mac** drive a Windows VM in Google Cloud over SSH: it launches the app there, takes screenshots, sends scripted clicks, and copies the results back. It's at `/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/`, and it was verified end to end on 2026-09-07, including compiling JusPrin from source on that VM (deps 23 min, slicer 23 min) and screenshotting the built binary with its Agent UI visible.

The VM (`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`, now n2-standard-16) currently exists but is **stopped**. Its external IP is ephemeral, so starting it means re-reading the IP and updating `winssh.sh`/`winscp.sh` in the harness directory.

## Why not remote desktop from the Mac

Remote desktop is the worst of the three for this particular app:

- **Screenshots through RDP go through a pixel-scraping layer twice.** I'd be driving a Microsoft Remote Desktop window with generic screen-control tools, reading a scaled-down image of a scaled window. Verifying that a control is 26px tall or a corner radius is 4px — the kind of thing your recent UI work turns on — becomes unreliable.
- **RDP creates its own Windows session, and disconnecting tears it down or locks it.** Windows only lets display APIs see the calling session's desktop. The harness solves this by running UI work as a scheduled task pinned to the auto-logged-in console session, which survives having no one connected. RDP fights that design rather than using it.
- **It's slow.** Every click is a round trip through a video stream instead of a PowerShell call.

## Why not (usually) install Claude Code on the VM

It would work, but it buys little and costs setup: a second checkout of the repo on Windows, authenticating Claude Code there, and keeping the two copies in sync. The long builds — the one thing a local agent would help with — are already handled by running them as Windows scheduled tasks, because OpenSSH kills the process tree when the connection drops.

The one case where installing it on the VM genuinely pays off is a **Windows-only compile bug that needs many edit-compile-read-error cycles**, like the MSVC lambda-capture error we hit. Over SSH each cycle is edit on Mac → copy → build → read log. An agent living on the VM shortens that loop. If you hit a run of those, install it then; it isn't worth doing preemptively.

## Recommendation

Stay on the Mac and use the existing harness. If you want, I can start the VM, refresh the IP, and run a look-and-behave pass on the current `jusprin-newui` build — tell me whether to build the branch fresh on the VM (~45 min) or install a binary you already have.

For some reason, on my Mac, when the AI agents need to test UI, the novin often takes over the entire screen, and it looks like when I move my mouse to use my Mac even on another screen it'll interfere with the AI agent testing. Check online to see if it's actually true or it's just my hallucinating.

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac; the App Store copy and other worktree builds share the bundle id, so run a re-signed copy under its own bundle id for screenshots."
metadata:
  type: project
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

## Key Finding on Cursor Movement

The basic approach to synthetic clicking on macOS using CGEventPost with LeftMouseDown and LeftMouseUp also moves the cursor. CGEventPost drops the event into the HID event stream (the same stream your physical mouse uses), and WindowServer sees a click at a coordinate and updates the pointer to that location as a side effect.

This is directly relevant to your query: CGEventPost drops the event into the HID event stream, which is the same stream your physical mouse uses. # User Mouse Movement and Agent Automation on macOS

The article directly addresses this concern:

**Single Shared Cursor Problem:**
The traditional approach fails because "it also moves the cursor. `CGEventPost` drops the event into the HID event stream, which is the same stream your physical mouse uses."

**The Solution - postToPid:**
Using `CGEvent.postToPid` routes events to a specific process instead of the global HID stream, achieving "No cursor warp." This means agent clicks don't move the physical cursor that the user controls.

**Key Distinction:**
The article explains that the user's cursor and the agent's synthetic cursor operate independently. Agent automation doesn't interfere with physical mouse movement because it bypasses the shared HID event stream entirely.

**Multi-Cursor Approach:**
Rather than a separate session, cua-driver implements what the article calls "multi-cursor background agents"—allowing an agent to drive applications backgrounded while the user maintains independent foreground control without their focus or cursor position being affected.

**Direct Quote:**
"The cursor doesn't move. Focus doesn't change. macOS doesn't follow the agent across Spaces."

This architecture solves the interference problem by treating agent input and user input as separate control paths rather than competing for the same system resources.

content.text:
You're not hallucinating. Two of your three observations are real and have a documented mechanism; the third — "even on another screen" — is real but for a different reason than you'd guess.

Some background for a cold reader: when an automated agent clicks on a Mac, it creates a fake mouse event in software. There are two different ways to deliver it, and they behave very differently with respect to your physical mouse.

## The app taking over the screen

That one is deliberate, not a glitch. To screenshot and click a window, the automation brings that app to the front first. JusPrin/OrcaSlicer opens a large window, so "frontmost" looks like "took over the screen."

## Why your mouse interferes

The common way to send a synthetic click is `CGEventPost`, which **injects the event into the same HID event stream your physical mouse uses**, and as a side effect the system warps the real cursor to the click coordinate. So the agent's clicks and your hand are literally driving one cursor. If you move the mouse between the moment the agent decides where to click and the moment it clicks, you can land somewhere else.

It cuts both ways: macOS has a **local events suppression interval, 0.25 seconds by default** — after a synthetic event is posted, real hardware mouse input is ignored for a quarter second. That's why your own mouse also feels sticky or laggy while an agent is clicking.

## The other-display part

Moving the mouse to another display does **not** change which app is frontmost. macOS tracks focus at the application level and changes it on a click, not on hover — the existence of a whole cottage industry of "focus follows mouse" utilities is the evidence that it isn't the default.

But there is only **one cursor shared across all displays**. So moving it on your second monitor is still moving the exact cursor the agent is trying to warp. And if you *click* over there, the frontmost app changes, and any keystrokes the agent sends to "the focused app" land in your app instead. That's the case that silently corrupts a test run.

## What to do about it

The fix is to stop using the shared cursor. `CGEvent.postToPid` delivers the event **to one process directly**, with no cursor warp and no focus change — the referenced write-up puts it as: "The cursor doesn't move. Focus doesn't change."

Practically, for our work:

- **Keyboard-driven testing is already immune.** We verified on 2026-09-07 that posting key events straight to the app's process ID drives it — it sliced on Cmd+R and reached the Upload-and-Print button by Tab/Arrow/Space — *with the screen locked*. Your mouse cannot interfere with that path at all.
- **Prefer per-app clicks over screen-coordinate clicks.** The per-application click tool appears to deliver into the app rather than through the shared cursor (a screen-coordinate click failed to open the fork's popup menus, while the per-app click opened them) — I'm inferring the mechanism from that behavior, not from documentation.
- **Screenshots are the part that still needs the screen.** Mouse events posted directly to the process did nothing in our test, and screen capture fails outright when the Mac is locked.
- **If you want real isolation, use the Windows VM** we discussed, or a second machine. Nothing on your Mac's desk contends with it.

Sources: [Inside macOS window internals — Cua](https://cua.ai/blog/inside-macos-window-internals), [CGEventSourceSetLocalEventsSuppressionInterval — Apple](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coregraphics/1408783-cgeventsourcesetlocaleventssuppr), [Mac games and cursor warping weirdness — Colin Cornaby](https://www.colincornaby.me/2023/02/mac-games-and-cursor-warping-weirdness/), [MouseFollowsFocus](https://github.com/dekstop/MouseFollowsFocus)
